text:
sam_customer: Hey team — customer reports /v1/rerank calls failing after copy-pasting the cURL from Console. They said it worked for a quick test in the browser, but when they run the exact command in Windows cmd they get a 400. Paste below (they literally pasted this):

sam_customer: ```
curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/rerank' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"Which product is cheaper?","candidates":["Prod A","Prod B"]}'
```

jess_support: Thanks — two quick things: does the customer run that in cmd.exe or PowerShell? The single quotes in the Console snippet are bash-friendly and will break on Windows cmd. Also, the error body from the API would help (the raw JSON error).

sam_customer: They said cmd.exe. Error they pasted: "400 Bad Request: invalid JSON payload - unexpected character at position 1". Also noted that when they tried a different snippet, the reranker returned identical scores for every candidate (0.0 / 1.0-ish).

carlos_engineer: Copying here — there are two separate failure modes:
1) Quoting/escaping on Windows leads to malformed JSON being sent (hence 400). Console examples often use single quotes which cmd.exe treats as normal characters.
2) If clients send the wrong field shape (we expect: a top-level JSON object with `query` and `candidates` array — each candidate should be a string or object with an `id` field), the server may fall back to default scoring behavior, which can look like "flat" or identical scores.

For repro (cmd.exe) use this exact command (note the escaped double quotes):
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/rerank" ^
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" ^
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" ^
  -d "{\"query\":\"Which product is cheaper?\",\"candidates\":[\"Prod A\",\"Prod B\"]}"
```

For PowerShell use this:
```
curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/rerank' 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -Body (@{query="Which product is cheaper?"; candidates=@("Prod A","Prod B")} | ConvertTo-Json)
```

marta_docs: Good catch — Console samples are rendered assuming a POSIX shell. I'll open a docs PR to add an explicit Windows/cmd.exe snippet and a note that the Console copy button currently outputs single-quote examples. We should also add an example showing the candidate objects shape (string vs {id,text}).

jess_support: Thanks @marta_docs. @sam_customer can you ask the customer to try the cmd.exe sample above and paste the raw response (not screenshot)? If they still see identical scores, ask them to include the exact request JSON they sent and their candidate list size — we have a hard limit at 75 candidates currently and hitting that can trigger an error or degrade scoring.

sam_customer: Will do — forwarding now. They also said one more oddity: when they sent candidates as objects like `{id:1,text:"Prod A"}` the server returned a 200 but the "scores" array length was zero.

carlos_engineer: If they send candidate objects, they must be valid JSON (keys in double quotes) and include either `text` or `content` per the schema. Example good payload: `{"query":"Which product is cheaper?","candidates":[{"id":"a1","text":"Prod A"},{"id":"b2","text":"Prod B"}]}`. Missing `text` can produce a successful 200 with an empty scores array because the model had nothing to score.

marta_docs: I'll add both a minimal bash, PowerShell, and Windows cmd snippet + a small note about maximum candidate limits and valid candidate object shape. Also adding a tiny troubleshooting checklist we can paste into support replies.

jess_support: Perfect — once docs PR is live, I'll reply to the customer with the corrected cURL and a repro checklist (1) which shell they used, (2) full request body, (3) response body, (4) number of candidates. If this still repros, escalate to eng with request id and request/response pair.

sam_customer: Customer tried the cmd.exe command and it succeeded. Thanks — they said updating the Console examples would avoid future confusion. :thumbsup:
